shortName: Charles E. Schmidt College of Medicine at Florida Atlantic University
additionalCoursework:
Recommended courses: 3 credit hours in Behavioral Sciences and Computer Science, and 6 credit hours in Social Sciences and Humanities.
Required courses: 6 credit hours in College English, and 8 credit hours in Inorganic and Organic Chemistry (preferably taken within 5 years of the application date).

medSchoolStudLife.diversity: Diversity and inclusion are core values of the Charles E. Schmidt College of Medicine. We believe diversity and inclusion are driving forces and indicators of excellence and innovation in academic medicine. The purpose of our office is to create programs and an environment that will promote the development and success of our diverse students, faculty, staff and community.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: The College of Medicine currently has over 20 student organizations on campus. We have chapters of both the American Medical Student Association and American Medical Women's Association. There are also a wide variety of specialty interest groups including Surgery Interest Group, Internal Medicine Interest Group, and Pediatrics Interest Group which present guest lecturers to the student body and actively participate in community service. We also have two intramural teams composed entirely of medical students who play weekly games of soccer and basketball.
medSchoolStudLife.setting: The College of Medicine is located on the sub-tropical campus of Florida Atlantic University in suburban Boca Raton, Florida, only a mile from the Atlantic Ocean and its beautiful beaches.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: A variety of affordable housing options are available.  Housing is available on campus and close to the College of Medicine; most students however live in off-campus apartment complexes within 2-3 miles of the College.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems:
At the FAU College of Medicine, we support and promote diversity and inclusiveness. We work hard to create a health workforce of physicians and scientists capable of delivering high quality, equitable health care to all Americans and capable of eliminating health disparities, in not only our local communities, but globally as well.
We have also created programs and policies to ensure not only the racial, ethnic and cultural diversity, but also the cognitive diversity of its students, faculty, and staff. Diversity goes beyond race and ethnicity and includes factors such as gender, educational background, individual achievement, research experience, non-traditional academic backgrounds, socioeconomic disadvantage, and other life adversity.
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: The campus culture at the FAU Schmidt College of Medicine is built on collaboration, inclusivity, and a strong commitment to serving the community. With small class sizes, students benefit from close relationships with faculty, fostering a supportive learning environment where mentorship and professional growth are prioritized. The college emphasizes hands-on clinical experience, innovative research, and a curriculum integrating compassion with scientific excellence. Students are encouraged to engage in service-learning initiatives, diversity-focused programs, and interdisciplinary teamwork, all of which contribute to a well-rounded medical education. FAU’s vibrant and diverse community creates an atmosphere where future physicians can develop both the technical skills and the humanistic qualities necessary to become healthcare leaders.

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode: Casual for classroom work, professional dress for all sessions with patients
medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: Faculty have office hours and tutoring is available.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Students are assigned to preceptors in the community for weekly clinical exposure at the end of the 1st semester after an intensive clinical skills course to prep them for hands-on patient encounters.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Very hands on with lots of small group, PBL,TBL, and simulation activities
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: At the Florida Atlantic University Charles E. Schmidt College of Medicine we have implemented a longitudinal integrated curriculum in the third year.
medSchoolCurriculum.prematriculationProgram: Biochemistry and Immunology Modules are recommended for all students and required for identified students.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: The Integrated Patient Focused Curriculum features an active learning style using problem-based approaches and early patient contact. This begins in the first days of medical school when students visit community health centers and interview patients about their illnesses, treatments, and life changes. The acquisition of clinical skills begins in our Simulation Center and is augmented continuously through patient interactions under the tutelage of community preceptors. The third year features longitudinal integrated clerkships in which students are placed at clinical sites for up to 6 months and become active members of the health care team, learning about the system of care while developing core competencies for residency. The curriculum emphasizes humanistic medicine, professionalism, evidence-based decision making, comprehensive management of chronic diseases, and inter-professional teamwork in addressing each patient's needs.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: All our students participate in a longitudinal primary care preceptor experience  called the Community and Preventive Medicine Clerkship. We do not have a separate primary care track but are thinking of launching one.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: FAU has a very robust MD/PhD program; our afiliation with Max Plank Florida provides a myriad of opportunities for students to conduct research
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: We have a mandatory service learning project as part of the M1-M2 curriculum
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: Cleveland Clinic Florida, Joe DiMaggio Children's Hospital, Memorial Hospital System, Boca Raton Regional Hospital, Delray Medical Center, West Boca Medical Center, West Palm Beach VA Medical Center,
medSchoolCurriculum.gradingSystem:
Pass/ Fail years 1 and 2 and 4.
Honors, High Pass, Pass, Fail for year 3 clerkships

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: The College's curriculum features a small class size with individual attention and a collegial student-centered learning environment; emphasis on small-group and self-directed learning; early clinical experiences; required service-learning projects; and longitudinal integrated clerkships for all its students in the third year, with rotations at prominent hospitals in Palm Beach and Broward counties. The Schmidt College of Medicine is one of the newest and rapidly rising medical schools in the United States, nationally recognized by U.S. News and World Report for its mission to care for diverse patient populations. To serve the community, the college maintains partnerships with more than 300 community agencies from Miami-Dade to Vero Beach, Florida. With an emphasis on teamwork and collaboration, the college is dedicated to addressing the needs of its community. **Our college does not consider any transfer requests or advanced standing due to the unique integration of our curriculum.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement: Our mission extends beyond training the next generation of physicians – we aim to transform healthcare delivery in South Florida and beyond. We will achieve this through our commitment to innovative medical education, groundbreaking research, and exceptional patient care. By fostering an environment that encourages scientific discovery and clinical excellence, with a focus on evidence-based care, we prepare our learners to become not just skilled physicians, but healthcare leaders who will shape the future of medicine.
medSchoolInformation.programUndergradCollege: The Schmidt College of Medicine offers programs which allow outstanding students the opportunity to achieve their B.S. and M.D. degrees in 7-8 years. Students admitted into these highly selective programs will be offered conditional admission* to the Schmidt College of Medicine provided they maintain the required program standards. Each student will work closely with the programs' faculty and staff to develop an individual education plan and to ensure a smooth transition if accepted into the College of Medicine.
medSchoolInformation.programAbout:
Program Highlights: 
1. During the spring of their senior year, select high school finalists are offered an interview at the College of Medicine.
2. Students enrolled in the B.S./M.D. programs will receive mentoring from medical students and faculty from the College of Medicine.
3. Students will participate in meaningful research, volunteer, and medical experiences.
4. Students will have the opportunity to interact with the College of Medicine and its affiliate hospitals.
5. Students will be provided individualized pre-medical advising throughout the entire undergraduate program.

medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText: All letters of recommendation must be sent from AMCAS. Since our admissions process is electronic, letters mailed/emailed from the writer or hand-delivered directly to the Office of Admissions cannot be added to the applicant's file and, therefore, will not be used in the admissions process. Schmidt COM prefers to receive a committee letter through AMCAS authored by a pre-health committee or pre-health advisor which is a composite or summary evaluation of the applicant's readiness and personal suitability to study medicine. Alternatively, letters may be sent to us from AMCAS as part of a "letter packet", or individually. In either case, we require a minimum of three letters from faculty members who have taught the applicant. Two of these letters must be written by science faculty members while the third can be written by either a science or non-science faculty member.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance: Letters of recommendation (LORs) are vital to the medical school application, offering insight into your academic abilities, clinical experiences, and character. Additionally to the required letter, a clinical letter from a physician or healthcare professional is highly beneficial. If you have research experience, a letter from your research mentor is recommended. Also, a Committee Letter, if your institution provides one, and optional letters from employers or volunteer supervisors can add value. Choosing recommenders who know you well is crucial, as they can provide specific examples of your strengths, work ethic, and passion for medicine. Request letters at least two to three months before deadlines, preferably in person or via a polite, professional email. Providing your resume, personal statement, and key points for them to highlight will help them craft a strong letter. Be sure to communicate deadlines and submission instructions.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay:
Formal interview days are scheduled on Tuesdays and Thursdays (some Mondays) between August and March. Interview days begin with introductory presentations, interviews, current medical student panels, and video tours.

Each applicant will have a situational-behavioral style format. A video tour of the simulation center and the teaching facilities is included. A "What will happen next?" presentation by the director of admissions will give applicants a timeline for when they hear back. Formal interview days begin at 9:00 am EST and end in the mid-afternoon, around 3 PM EST.
medSchoolApplication.interviewInvitations: Invitations are sent on a rolling basis. Starting in August, they are emailed; applicants should check their inbox regularly. If invited, applicants should promptly schedule their interviews.
medSchoolApplication.videoInterview: SparkHire asynchronous interviews are used in addition to a live interview on Zoom.
medSchoolApplication.secApplSentTo: All US citizens and permanent residents who submit a verified AMCAS application. Applicants with a felony explanation on their AMCAS application are not sent a secondary application.
medSchoolApplication.ctsRequired: Charles E. Schmidt College of Medicine admits approximately 30% of its students from states other than Florida.
medSchoolApplication.stateResAfterMatric: A Florida resident for tuition purposes at FAUCOM is a person who has established and maintained legal residence in Florida for at least 12 consecutive months immediately prior to initial enrollment
medSchoolApplication.acceptOutstateApplInformation: 30% of the class will be out-of -state applicants.
medSchoolApplication.acceptCanadianApplInformation: Must at least be a permiment resident of the US in order to be considered for admissions.
medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
Each completed application (AMCAS application, letters of recommendation, MCAT score, secondary application) will be screened and scored by a team of evaluators within the College of Medicine. Schmidt COM takes pride in conducting a Holistic Review of applications submitted. Factors evaluated at this point include the applicant’s attributes, community service, values, educational background, GPAs, MCAT scores, the rigor of the educational program(s) undertaken, breadth of life experiences, research, and, yet not limited to the meaningfulness of direct patient contact experiences as well as other experiences.

The scores assessed in the screening process will be used to send invitations for an interview with the College of Medicine.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo: The Admissions Committee pays attention to all subscores, yet, really emphasizes the CARS section of the exam.
medSchoolApplication.minUndergradGpaInfo: A cumulative and BCPM GPA of 3.5 is considered competitive.
medSchoolApplication.minCreditHourInfo: preferred 3.7 graduate or post bacc GPA
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: Community College coursework is accepted as long as the applicant has performed well and shows an upward trend.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: Letters of interest are only accepted from applicants placed on the alternate list (waitlist). Letters can be emailed to the Director of Admissions and addressed to the Admissions Committee. Letters of Interest are accepted from October 15th through April 30th. Letters of Intent can only be sent if you have been placed on the alternate list (waitlist) starting May 1st until July 15th. Letters of Intent must be emailed to the Director of Admissions.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo: The medical degree awarded by the College of Medicine at the completion of the undergraduate medical education process certifies that the graduate has acquired a broad base of knowledge, skills, and attitudes requisite to the practice of medicine. To achieve this end, all courses in the curriculum must be completed successfully. The technical (non-academic) standards listed here are required for admission, retention, promotion, and graduation and are intended to ensure that candidates, with or without reasonable accommodation, can fully participate in all parts of the curriculum.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid:
FAU Schmidt College of Medicine applicants and students who wish to be considered for any type of financial assistance (grants, loans, scholarships, etc.) must complete the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA).

Students’ Cost of Attendance (COA) budgets are developed each academic year by the Office of Medical Student Financial Aid. They include Tuition and Fees (as approved by FAU’s governing boards); an allowance for books and supplies; and a cost of living allowance for Room and Board, Transportation, and Personal Expenses (see definitions, below). COA’s are estimated during the early awarding process and are subject to change once FAU’s governing boards finalize each year’s tuition and fee charges.

The COA, in conjunction with the students’ Expected Family Contribution (EFC) from their FAFSA’s, is used to both calculate financial aid eligibility and to give students an estimate of reasonable costs to attend the FAU College of Medicine.

medSchoolPrograms.info: The Pre-Health Professions Office's primary mission is to be a source of support and guidance for students interested in pursuing any career as medical, veterinary, dental, or physician assistant school candidates. Our pre-health advisors are committed to providing advice tailored to meet the needs of each individual and create meaningful relationships with our students. We work to create an environment full of academic excellence, strong relationships with students, faculty, and staff, and learning opportunities through clinical experiences, community service, scientific inquiry, and research, as well as campus involvement.

medSchoolPrograms.name: Max Planck Florida Institute for Neuroscience (MPFI)
medSchoolPrograms.deadline: After you have summitted your AMCAS to FAU

medSchoolPrograms.info: The Florida Atlantic University (FAU) Charles E. Schmidt Colleges of Medicine and Science and Max Planck Florida Institute for Neuroscience (MPFI) have created a M.D./Ph.D. dual degree program that provides talented students with cutting-edge training to become physician-scientists. The program allows students to complete their Ph.D. research in one of MPFI’s state of the art research groups while simultaneously earning their medical degree from FAU’s College of Medicine and doctoral degree from FAU’s Integrative Biology Ph.D. program. This collaborative M.D./Ph.D. program combines the rigorous academic curriculum and top-tier clinical training offered by FAU with the cutting-edge neuroscience research in laboratories at MPFI, which is part of the world-renowned Max Planck Society.  Students in the M.D./Ph.D. program follow a novel sequence of study at FAU and MPFI that promotes the distinct career path and integrated training in medicine and neuroscience research.

medSchoolTimeline.eventDetail: As for selecting "Plan-to-Enroll", please refer to the AMCAS PTE date and AAMC Applicant guidelines.

If choosing our medical school, Accepted applicants must select 'Commit to Enroll.' by June 16th. For more information regarding FAU COM policies on Choose Your Medical School tools, please get in touch with the Admissions Office at mdadmissions@health.fau.edu or visit our website.

medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistProcedure: Once it is determined seats are available with the College, applicants are reviewed by the Committee on Admissions. The waitlist is not ranked, therefore all applications are re-reviewed.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec: Prerequisite coursework should be completed in the US or Canada.  Required courses taken abroad will be considered only if a university in North America awards credits for such courses and  are included on the official transcript. Substitutions for required courses will be considered on a case by case basis.  CLEP credits are not acceptable as prerequisite coursework.
medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: The Committee on Admissions prefers prerequisite courses be completed no more than 5 years of application cycle with a grade of a C or better.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: Only United States citizens and permanent residents are accepted. Although residents of Florida are given preference, up to 30% of the class may come from other states. Selection factors include classroom performance, MCAT scores, quality of letters of recommendation, meaningfulness of direct patient contact experiences, diversity of background, volunteer and community service; research; and an assessment of personal traits such as maturity, responsibility, integrity, respect for others, altruism and intellectual curiosity in an interview.
